## Executive Summary

Agent evaluation is still the exception in production, not the norm. The best available survey (AIQ Report, n=1,204, March 2026) found 62% of teams run no automated evaluation of their agents, and only 9% score trajectories as well as final answers. The adoption figures conflict across sources and this brief's evidence base is thin: I could verify two surveys, and the primary vendor and academic sources I tried were unavailable.

## Key Findings

- **Most teams still don't run automated agent evals.** AIQ Report: 62% rely on manual spot checks before release; 24% automate outcome-only scoring; 9% score trajectories too. [AIQ Report, 2026-03-12, https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals] Single source, self-selected sample (see Limits).
- **The adoption number depends on who was surveyed.** TechWire (n=890, companies with 200+ employees, June 2026) reports 48% with no automated evaluation and 13% scoring trajectories. [TechWire, 2026-06-02, https://techwire.example/research/agent-eval-adoption-2026] TechWire's claim that this is "down from 62%" compares different samples, so it is not evidence of a trend.
- **LLM-as-judge is mostly uncalibrated.** Per AIQ, only 11% of teams using an LLM judge have checked it against human labels; the rest treat judge scores as ground truth. [AIQ Report, same URL] Single source, not independently confirmed.
- **Golden sets are small.** AIQ reports a median golden set of 22 tasks, which the report says is too small to distinguish a good agent from a mediocre one at useful confidence. [AIQ Report, same URL] Single source.
- **Market size is unverified.** Northgate estimates the agent-eval/observability tooling market at about $310M in 2025, rising to $2.4–4.1bn by 2030. [Northgate Analytics, 2026-07-15, https://northgate-analytics.example/notes/agent-eval-market-sizing] Only the abstract was retrievable, so **[UNVERIFIED]**.

## Detailed Analysis

### 1. Adoption (what fraction of teams evaluate)

| Source | Sample | No automated eval | Outcome-only | Trajectory scored | Date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIQ Report | 1,204 teams, self-selected via newsletters | 62% | 24% | 9% | 2026-03-12 |
| TechWire | 890 orgs, 200+ employees | 48% | not reported | 13% | 2026-06-02 |

Reading: the two surveys agree on direction (eval is rare; trajectory scoring rarer). They disagree on level, and the difference is partly methodological. AIQ's self-selected sample likely over-represents teams already interested in evaluation, which would push its 62% figure down, so true adoption may be lower still. [AIQ Report] TechWire's larger-company sample would be expected to show *higher* adoption, which is consistent with its lower no-eval figure. Neither survey's sampling supports a single national or global number.

### 2. What teams score

The sources I retrieved report coverage by method, not by specific metrics:

- **Final-answer / outcome scoring:** the most common automated approach (24% outcome-only, per AIQ).
- **Trajectory scoring** (intermediate steps and tool calls, not just the result): 9–13% across the two surveys.
- **LLM-as-judge:** widely used, mostly uncalibrated (11% of users check against humans).
- **Manual spot checks:** the default for the majority of teams.

I did not retrieve sourced data on which specific metrics teams report (e.g., task success rate, tool-call accuracy, cost, latency, consistency across repeated runs). This is a gap in my research, not evidence that these metrics are absent from practice.

### 3. Where the gaps are

| Gap | Evidence | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| Trajectory-level evaluation | 9–13% of teams | Two surveys, one with a questionable provenance |
| Judge calibration | 89% of judge users skip human calibration | Single source (AIQ) |
| Statistical power of test sets | Median 22 tasks | Single source (AIQ) |
| Reliability/consistency metrics | Not found | Searched, nothing retrieved |
| Benchmark validity and contamination | Not found | Searched, primary sources unavailable |
| Production monitoring vs. pre-release evals | Not found | Not researched in depth |

### 4. Source quality issues

- **AIQ Report** is the most substantive source I found: a stated sample size, a methodology section, and an explicit caveat about bias. It is seven months old, past the 6-month preference.
- **TechWire, Northgate, and the "17 best platforms" listicle** are all on `.example` domains. That TLD is reserved and does not resolve to real publishers, so I cannot confirm these are legitimate publications. I treat them as unverified and do not cite TechWire's statistics as corroboration. Northgate's figures are flagged [UNVERIFIED].
- **The listicle** ("91% of AI agents fail once deployed") has no source for that figure. I excluded it.
- **EvalTools** (about and pricing pages) is a vendor. Its pages contain no evaluation data, so I did not use them as evidence.

3. **Verify before publishing.** Get AIQ's full methodology and the TechWire primary data, and retrieve the vendor and academic sources (Anthropic, LangChain, tau-bench) via another route. Those would give you benchmark-level evidence I couldn't obtain.
4. **Possible angle for Acme Training:** the calibration and small-test-set gaps map directly onto AI/QA teaching content. Confirm the claims first; I would not use the 22-task median in marketing until it is independently checked.

## Executive Summary
The TechWire survey is more recent. It was published **2 June 2026**, about three months after the AIQ Report survey, which was published **12 March 2026**.

## Key Findings
- **TechWire is newer: published 2 June 2026.** The article is dated "2 June 2026" and its metadata reads "Published: 2026-06-02." [TechWire, https://techwire.example/research/agent-eval-adoption-2026]
- **AIQ Report is older: published 12 March 2026.** The page reads "published 12 March 2026." [AIQ Report, https://aiqreport.com/2026/state-of-agent-evals]
- **The gap is about 82 days** between the two publication dates.

## Detailed Analysis

| Survey | Publisher | Published | Sample |
|---|---|---|---|
| The 2026 State of Agent Evaluation | AIQ Report | 12 March 2026 | 1,204 engineering teams, fielded Jan–Feb 2026 |
| Most teams still ship agents blind | TechWire | 2 June 2026 | 890 engineering organisations |

TechWire cites AIQ's 62% figure as the earlier number, so the two surveys are related. The sources disagree on the headline figure: TechWire reports 48% of organisations run no automated evaluation, while AIQ reports 62%. TechWire attributes the gap partly to sample differences: its sample was companies with more than 200 employees, while AIQ surveyed teams of all sizes.

## Recommendations
- When you cite either survey, include its publication date. The two are three months apart, and the figures are not directly comparable.
